content: Before initiating treatment with ibrexafungerp, it is essential to confirm the pregnancy status of females of reproductive potential. The safety and efficacy of ibrexafungerp have not been established in premenarchal patients. Ibrexafungerp interacts with several drugs by affecting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to increased levels or effects of these drugs. For example: 1. Elacestrant: Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Etrasimod: Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Nirogacestat: Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Omaveloxolone: Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose to 100 mg/day and monitor for adverse effects. If adverse effects occur, further reduce the dose to 50 mg/day. 5. Pacritinib: Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Repotrectinib: Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 7. Tovorafenib: Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining tovorafenib (a CYP2C8 substrate) with strong or moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. 8. Atogepant: Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Capivasertib: Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 10. Daprodustat: Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the starting dose by half if coadministered, except when the starting dose is already 1 mg. Monitor hemoglobin levels and adjust the dose as needed. 11. Daridorexant: Modify therapy and monitor closely. The dose should not exceed 25 mg per night when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 12. Finererone: Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustments of either finererone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust the dosage as needed. 13. Gepirone: Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the dose by 50% when used with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 14. Isavuconazonium sulfate: Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Lumateperone: Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the dose to 21 mg/day if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Mavacamten: Modify therapy and monitor closely. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a reduced mavacamten dose. 17. Mavorixafor: Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor for adverse effects and reduce the daily dose if necessary. 18. Norgestrel: Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations, raising the risk of adverse effects. 19. Palovarotene: Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the dose by 50%. 20. Resmetirom: Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the dose when used with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. 21. Seladelpar: Use caution and monitor closely. Exercise caution in CYP2C9 poor metabolizers taking seladelpar and coadministered with moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 22. Sparsentan: Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Vardenafil: Modify therapy and monitor closely. The dose may need to be reduced when coadministered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Voclosporin: Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with drugs associated with nephrotoxicity may increase the risk of acute or chronic nephrotoxicity. 25. Zanubrutinib: Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the dose to 80 mg twice daily when coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Interrupt the dose as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous dose. Ibrexafungerp is contraindicated during pregnancy due to potential fetal harm based on animal data. There is insufficient data on its use in pregnant females to assess risks of major birth defects, miscarriage, or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. For females of reproductive potential, verify pregnancy status before initiating treatment and reassess before each dose if used monthly for six months to reduce recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis (RVVC). at 1-888-982-SCYX (7299). There is no data on the presence of ibrexafungerp in human or animal milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. Ibrexafungerp is a triterpenoid antifungal agent that inhibits glucan synthase, an enzyme involved in forming 1,3-beta-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall. It exhibits concentration-dependent fungicidal activity against Candida species, as demonstrated in time-kill studies. It is primarily metabolized by hydroxylation via CYP3A4, followed by glucuronidation and sulfation of an inactive hydroxylated metabolite. Its half-life is approximately 20 hours, and it is excreted mainly in feces (90%, with 51% unchanged) and urine (1%). It can be taken with or without food. Tablets should be stored at 20-25°C (68-77°F), with excursions permitted to 15-30°C (59-86°F).
